sequences.title: Incident management steps
sequences.prompt: Put the incident management steps in the order the ISC2 study guide teaches.
sequences.note: Mitigation contains the incident. Reporting starts early and continues; remediation fixes the root cause after systems are recovered, and lessons learned closes the loop.

sequences.title: Business continuity planning
sequences.prompt: Order the phases of the business continuity planning process.
sequences.note: Scope and sponsorship first; the BIA sets priorities; strategies follow; senior management approves before roll-out.

sequences.title: Business impact analysis
sequences.prompt: Order the steps of a business impact analysis.
sequences.note: What matters most comes first, then what threatens it, how likely and how damaging, and finally where to spend.

sequences.title: NIST Risk Management Framework
sequences.prompt: Order the steps of the NIST RMF (SP 800-37 Rev. 2).
sequences.note: Prepare was added in Rev. 2. A system is authorized only after its controls are assessed, then monitored continuously.

sequences.title: System development life cycle
sequences.prompt: Order the phases of the system development life cycle.
sequences.note: Security requirements are set at initiation and carried through every phase, including secure disposal.

sequences.title: Forensic process
sequences.prompt: Order the phases of the forensic process in NIST SP 800-86.
sequences.note: Collect while preserving integrity, examine to extract relevant data, analyze it to draw conclusions, then report.

sequences.title: Order of volatility
sequences.prompt: Order evidence sources from most volatile (collect first) to least volatile (RFC 3227).
steps: Memory: routing and ARP tables, process list
sequences.note: Collect what disappears soonest first. Powering a system off loses everything above the disk.

sequences.title: Disaster recovery tests
sequences.prompt: Order disaster recovery test types from least to most disruptive.
sequences.note: A parallel test runs the recovery site alongside production; only a full interruption actually shuts production down.

sequences.title: Change management
sequences.prompt: Order the steps of the change management process.
sequences.note: Even emergency changes go through review and documentation, just after the fact.

sequences.title: Kerberos logon
sequences.prompt: Order what happens when a Kerberos user reaches an application server.
steps: The client authenticates to the authentication service
The authentication service issues a ticket-granting ticket
The client presents the TGT to the ticket-granting service
The ticket-granting service issues a service ticket
The client presents the service ticket to the application server
sequences.note: The password never crosses the network. The TGT gets service tickets; the service ticket gets access.

sequences.title: OSI model
sequences.prompt: Order the OSI layers from layer 1 to layer 7.
sequences.note: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away.

sequences.title: Penetration test
sequences.prompt: Order the phases of a penetration test.
sequences.note: Planning includes written authorization and rules of engagement; nothing starts without them.

sequences.title: Data lifecycle
sequences.prompt: Order the phases of the data lifecycle (Cloud Security Alliance model).
sequences.note: Classification happens at creation; destruction must fit the media and the data's sensitivity.

sequences.title: Capability Maturity Model
sequences.prompt: Order the Software Capability Maturity Model levels from 1 to 5.
sequences.note: Repeatable brings basic project management; Managed adds quantitative measures; Optimizing improves continuously.

sequences.title: IDEAL model
sequences.prompt: Order the phases of the IDEAL software process improvement model.

sequences.title: Cyber kill chain
sequences.prompt: Order the stages of the Lockheed Martin cyber kill chain.
sequences.note: Defenders aim to break the chain as early as possible; the earlier the stage, the cheaper the stop.

sequences.title: PASTA threat modeling
sequences.prompt: Order the seven stages of PASTA.
sequences.note: PASTA is risk-centric: it starts from business objectives and ends with risk decisions.

sequences.title: Government classification
sequences.prompt: Order U.S. government classification levels from lowest to highest.
sequences.note: Unauthorized disclosure causes damage (Confidential), serious damage (Secret) or exceptionally grave damage (Top Secret) to national security.
